articles.title: 'The Movie Still Hasn't Made Any Money': Dakota Johnson is Happy to Joke About Madame Web Being One of Hollywood's Worst Ever Flops
articles.summary: Madame Web star Dakota Johnson has joked about her widely-panned superhero movie's status as a box office bomb. Appearing as the host of this week's Saturday Night Live, Johnson humorously noted that she had last fronted the show back in 2024 while promoting the Spider-Man spinoff.
body: "The last time I was here I was promoting a movie called Madame Web, thank you," Johnson said to muted applause. "And tonight I'm still promoting it because the movie still hasn't made any money yet."

Madame Web is infamously bad, even in a run of films from Sony that also includes Morbius and Venom 3. It made $100.5 million at the box office from a gross budget of $100 million (although factoring in distributor costs is believed to still made a loss). It was also a disaster critically: the subject of widespread memes online and a 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It later scooped three Golden Raspberry awards, including Worst Actress for Johnson herself.

While the film did not make a lot of cash, Madame Web is a long way from ranking among Hollywood's worst box office bombs — or even the worst-performing comic book movie. Disney's John Carter is widely-regarded as the biggest commercial failure of all time, losing up to $200 million. Disney's The Lone Ranger lost up to $190 million, meanwhile. Just behind those was The Marvels, which lost a similar amount and remains the worst-performing comic book movie ever — a fate Madame Web avoided by being far cheaper to make.
points: Madame Web star Dakota Johnson has joked about her widely-panned superhero movie's status as a box office bomb.
"The last time I was here I was promoting a movie called Madame Web, thank you," Johnson said to muted applause.

articles.title: Rockstar Traveled Across Florida With Gang Members and Cops for GTA 6 Research
articles.summary: Love Magazine recently got an exclusive interview with Rockstar Games ahead of GTA 6 ’s release next month. While the interview focuses primarily on the love story between dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, there’s some interesting insight into the studio’s process for creating the most impressive…
body: For its rendition of Florida, team members spent lots of time embedding with the culture and exploring the landscape of Miami and its surrounding areas. These research trips start small as the leads scout out the most interesting locations and stories, and more team members come on subsequent trips to dive deeper into the culture, stories, and people.

“Every game we make starts with research trips. It’s where to get to explore both the place and our ideas as a group,” head of development Aaron Garbut said. “To begin, a small group of us spent some time traveling from Miami through some of the surrounding towns and through the Florida Keys down to Key West. This is one of the best parts of the entire project: a car full of friends, driving for days on end, talking about what we want to make and being immersed in the locations and our ideas.”

Garbut takes a camera and a phone and records everything that happens. During one shoot, a handful of Rockstar devs spent the day flying low and fast over mangrove inlets in the everglades, before ending the day hovering over a stadium with a live Beyonce concert playing. “I think we made the local news that day,” Garbut said.
points: Love Magazine recently got an exclusive interview with Rockstar Games ahead of GTA 6 ’s release next month.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Resonance feels so good to play because Square Enix 'experimented' with combining the best bits of FF5 and FF6
articles.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance, a game made from the ashes of closed-down mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, is good. Very good, in fact, as I learned at Gamescom 2026. It's basically a pixel-first FF RPG that takes old-school turn-based combat and modernises it.
body: I have been thinking about the game since Gamescom, sinking five hours into the free demo that launched shortly afterwards. It's a great, modern reinterpretation of what 'classic' Final Fantasy looks like - and it turns out that was Square Enix 's intention all along, Final Fantasy Resonance director Hiroto Furuya told Kotaku in an interview. "As a foundation, it’s very important [that] we have knowledge of Final Fantasy's history and its past. But we're also gamers at heart, so of course we play the latest games that are available outside of Final Fantasy. We have the sensibility of knowing Final Fantasy's history, as well as the general feeling of playing more modern games".

Furuya went on to talk about the specific games the team has looked at when rethinking the combat system from Brave Exvius, considering how a pixel-first Final Fantasy should feel and play in the modern age. And it turns out the best place to look for inspiration were the last two pixel Final Fantasy titles in the mainline series: 1992's Final Fantasy 5 and 1994's Final Fantasy 6.
points: Final Fantasy Resonance, a game made from the ashes of closed-down mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, is good.

articles.title: GTA 6 Shows 'What the American Dream Looks Like Now' in a Game Without Background Characters
articles.summary: From what we've seen so far about Grand Theft Auto 6, it looks like one of the biggest open-world games in history. When developers have to create such sprawling virtual environments, there's a risk of them feeling empty or repetitive, but that doesn't seem to be the case with GTA 6.
body: Rockstar is known for paying attention to details that are easy to overlook. That was evident in Red Dead Redemption 2, where the world felt truly alive, and it will be even more so in Grand Theft Auto 6. According to the interview with Love Magazine, Rockstar sent teams to various parts of Florida to study not only the locations and environments, but also its people and culture. This will be reflected in NPCs' conversations, clothing, and hairstyles.

Players will be able to spend hours observing these NPCs and still find new details and conversations to overhear. NPCs are meant to go beyond background characters that players can just run over without a second thought; they actually have a life of their own, and gamers can get to know them simply by listening to what they have to say. "In a world this dense, no one you meet is an extra," says the Instagram caption of the post advertising the new issue of the magazine.
"In a way, there's no 'background' in this game," writing director James Horton said in the Love interview. "There's just foreground you're not paying attention to right now."
points: From what we've seen so far about Grand Theft Auto 6, it looks like one of the biggest open-world games in history.

articles.title: 31 Years Later, One of the Most Disturbing Thrillers Ever Made Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: Released in 1995, Ice Cream Man is the type of so-bad-it's-good horror movie that rarely gets made in the post- Get Out era where the genre is taken much more seriously.
body: Earlier this summer, Eli Roth released Ice Cream Man, a tedious, blood-soaked horror movie tarnished by AI slop and cringey dialogue. It's too bad, not just because I expected better from the director of Cabin Fever and Thanksgiving, but because Roth also sullied the good name of another schlocky horror movie with the exact same title that's a hell of a lot more fun to watch.

In other words, unlike the Eli Roth movie, the original Ice Cream Man is a B-movie horror masterpiece, and if you're looking for an absurd scary movie to get into the Halloween spirit, you truly can't do better than this.

Ice Cream Man stars Clint Howard (Ron Howard's younger brother) as Gregory Tudor, a severely troubled man who witnessed the murder of another ice cream truck driver when he was a child. Gregory winds up in a psychiatric institution where he receives treatment that verges on abuse. When he's finally released as an adult, he does the only logical thing: buy his own ice cream truck and start murdering people.

articles.title: RuneScape creator Jagex in hot water over generative AI use in recent trailer
articles.summary: RuneScape creator Jagex recently hosted its annual convention RuneFest, a hub for community events and new reveals for the British developer's many games. Sadly, one of those reveals has spoilt the fun somewhat due to unexpected generative AI use.
body: The trailer, a cinematic reveal for RuneScape 3's Dragon Slayer 2 quest, presents the premise for a new big adventure in a sketched style. However, people quickly spotted some strange issues with this trailer, such as a hand with six fingers, and a pair of fantasy Air Jordans.

This latest trailer coming in such short succession then isn't a good look for the developer, nor its stance against generative AI. Another statement was released in the wake of this trailer backlash, one that echoes much of the frustration from irked community members.

"We’re aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate urgently. This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there’s a sixth finger and, well, that’s pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise.

articles.title: Prime Video's Reacher Is Officially Returning This Month After a Stellar Season 4
articles.summary: If there’s one thing Reacher fans can count on, it’s that Jack Reacher is never gone for very long. The Prime Video series has turned Lee Child’s wandering ex-military cop into one of TV’s most reliably entertaining action heroes.
body: Not quite. Jack Reacher is already slated for a return this month, just not on television. Lee and Andrew Child are releasing a new novel in the exciting series called Chain Reaction, the 31st Jack Reacher outing, giving fans another dose of the beloved character before the show returns for its fifth season.

If Alan Ritchson ’s portrayal of the character has become one of your biggest TV obsessions, there’s never been a better moment to dive into the books. While the show does a fantastic job of introducing Lee Child’s iconic character — even better than the Tom Cruise movies — more than three decades of stories are waiting on the page. Child’s prose delivers a brand of pulse-pounding satisfaction for mystery buffs that the screen can only begin to match, and his latest offering is slated to be another exciting thrill ride.

articles.title: Lanterns Star Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan Is a Superhero Casting That Rivals Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man, Fans Say
articles.summary: Lanterns Season 1 is over, and the verdict is in: Fans say Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan rivals Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man as one of the best superhero casting choices of all time.
body: Fans had a lot on their minds as the DCU show's first season drew to a close. John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) will keep Earth safe whether Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) and the Guardians like it or not, and now, the planet has another Manhunter to worry about, too. It was a quieter final episode for Lanterns that did a lot of groundwork to set up the next chapter for its characters, but for now, at least, it truly seems Hal Jordan's story has come to an end.

Yes, it's true: Lanterns Season 1 suggests the DCU's Hal Jordan really, truly died in Rushville, Nebraska. It's a story beat that will no doubt leave at least some hardcore Green Lantern fans disappointed, no matter how hard Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) may have teased an option to bring him back to life. As the dust settles, though, the weight of Chandler's potential absence in the DCU proves that he left quite the mark on the Green Lantern name.

"Zero Reasons why they can't bring back Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan for a prequel," one fan hoped. "I don't care if it's a movie or show, or animated. You doing that writers' room for season 2 now? Yeah bring back Hal."
points: Lanterns Season 1 is over, and the verdict is in: Fans say Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan rivals Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man as one of the best superhero casting choices of all time.

articles.title: Arc Raiders is getting a free trial to celebrate its biggest update yet
articles.summary: Arc Raiders studio Embark is making the extraction shooter free to play for four days alongside the launch of the game's biggest update yet, Frozen Trail. The studio spent the last few days detailing all the new aspects of the update, and has now announced a way for players curious about the game…
body: The trial runs 8th to 12th October. Arc Raiders will be free to download and play across Steam, PlayStation and Xbox during that period. The trial surprisingly doesn't feature any locked content, with Embark saying it "grants access to the full Arc Raiders game".

That also extends to the new Pendola Pass map, which free weekend players can technically access immediately. That said, because the map needs to be unlocked by progressing through levels, it may take you a while to get there. Failing that, you can have a friend who already has Pendola Pass unlocked invite you to their squad.

Frozen Trail is expected to be a major moment for Arc Raiders. The expansion-size update adds a massive new map, several new Arc enemies and new weapons and gadgets. The update also marks the first major overhaul of the metagame, with tweaks to ammo, crafting and the addition of a more standard battle pass.

Arc Raiders has long since lost its massive launch audience, but I could see Frozen Trail being enough of a reason to lure players back. Given how much of the core game the update changes, Embark likely also sees it as the best entry point for new players.

articles.title: Lanterns Season 1 Finale Review & Recap
articles.summary: Though most of the twists can be seen coming well in advance, Lanterns Episode 8 manages to wrap up the season on an emotionally satisfying note.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 8!

A lot of burning questions have been hanging over the series in light of Episode 7, which changed the game by dragging John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and the Halogram to a war-ravaged alien world and inserting Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) back into the mix. Is this where the series blows the doors wide open in terms of the cosmic Green Lantern elements? Is Sinestro himself, not the mysteries in Rushville, the ultimate endgame of Season 1?

That all being said, the Noah of it all works well for me. No, the Manhunter reveal is not the most surprising direction the series could have taken. But as Christopher Nolan would argue, just because we can predict a plot twist ahead of time, that doesn’t automatically invalidate the story. Sometimes you just have to let these things play out as they should.
points: Though most of the twists can be seen coming well in advance, Lanterns Episode 8 manages to wrap up the season on an emotionally satisfying note.

articles.title: Warhammer: Blood Bowl is Blood Bowl 3.5 rather than a whole new game, but based on the beta it's definitely an upgrade
articles.summary: Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. A former music journalist who interviewed everyone from Giorgio Moroder to Trent Reznor, Jody also co-hosted Australia's first radio show about videogames,
body: It's a small thing, but being able to save and quit when I'm playing against the AI is a definite improvement in Warhammer: Blood Bowl. Though matches didn't take a huge amount of time in Blood Bowl 3, there were still nights where I'd find myself with 40 minutes before I should really go to bed thinking I can squeeze another game in, and then realizing too late I absolutely cannot.

A bigger change in Warhammer: Blood Bowl, though one that also makes it easier to squeeze in another match, is Rumble Mode. Based on the tabletop format called Sevens, it's a shrunk-down seven-a-side version of Blood Bowl played on a smaller pitch, inspired by 40K in 40 Minutes and Rugby Sevens. Each half has six turns instead of eight and rerolls cost twice as much, making failure much more common—and since a failed action results in a turnover in Blood Bowl, that speeds up play as well.

articles.title: RuneScape 4 is a new Unreal Engine MMO which reportedly grew out of a planned Dragonwilds expansion, though it's still a long way off
articles.summary: A fourth entry in the RuneScape series of MMOs has been announced by developers Jagex at this year's RuneFest. It's going by the obvious placeholder name of RuneScape 4 for now, is being developed using the Unreal Engine, and is still a decent way off.
body: "Still early in development, the as-yet-unnamed title will bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine," Jagex wrote of the next RuneScape. "Combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today."

Jagex's vice president of studios and next-gen development Jesse America revealed in a prebrief attended by MMORPG.com that this new MMO grew out of a planned 2027 expansion for survival spin-off RuneScape: Dragonwilds. The pitch has evolved into taking the worldstate or setting established by Dragonwilds and filling it with typical MMO features like persistent servers and trade hubs to form a fresh mainline entry.

"RS4 will be set in Gielinor, in the Sixth Age," Jagex confirmed in a post introducing the game. "But we're beginning somewhere that RuneScape players have only recently started to discover - and that is Ashenfall. An area first explored in RuneScape: Dragonwilds, and a landmass to the north-east of the Gielinor.

articles.title: It's easy to forget now, but the first Elder Scrolls game had a rough launch back in the day: 'It was a disaster in a lot of ways and somehow built a billion-dollar franchise'
articles.summary: Given the legacy it created, it's easy to forget The Elder Scrolls wasn't a big deal right out of the gate. The original game in the series, The Elder Scrolls: Arena, wasn't badly received—our reviewer, Andy Butcher, gave it an 87 in his review at the time—but it didn't set the world on fire…
body: In a retrospective on the making of Daggerfall over at Time Extension, Ted Peterson, designer on both the first two Elder Scrolls games, recalled the trouble Arena had moving copies when it first arrived on shelves in 1994.

"Game stores ordered a certain number of copies," he said, "and when we didn't ship on time, they started cancelling. To give you some context of how badly it did, the very, very first game I ever worked on was a retail pack for Terminator 2029, so you had to own the original game. That shipped more copies than Arena did early on. But we were lucky: word of mouth got out, and people started playing and enjoying the game. It was a disaster in a lot of ways and somehow built a billion-dollar franchise."

articles.title: "We opted out of some things really early on": How the small team making No Law plan to make it look as big as Cyberpunk 2077
articles.summary: If you've watched the trailers for No Law or the tech demo that developer Neon Giant showed off at Unreal Fest earlier this year, it would be easy to believe the game has a similar scope to CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077. After all, both games are open-world RPGs set in cyberpunk cities.
body: First thing on the table: Neon Giant are not as big as CD Project Red. One of No Law's creative directors, Tor Frick told me there are just 24 people working on the game. Now that number doesn't include the outsourcing teams helping with QA, art, and sound design, but even then, this is a smaller production. (Also, it's hardly new for developers to talk about games in this way, as Nic pointed out around the release of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. Still, Neon Giant knew their head count going into development and so it shaped a lot about the game that would become No Law.

Essentially, it looks like too much of a game to be made by 24 people. Even if it was actually made by slightly more than that, that's still wildly ambitious. However, as with any creative pursuit, Neon Giant recognised their limitations and designed them into the game.

"We opted out of some things really early on," Frick explains, pointing out that while you can see cars parked on the street, you won't be driving any of them. That both saves the team having to build out that functionality but it also reveals something about Port Desire's open world: "This is a city that is built to be navigated on foot," he says.
